newsitem.title: USA: S&P may change Rexene Corp ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P may change Rexene Corp ratings.

text.p: NEW YORK, Jan 2 - Standard & Poor's today has placed its double-B corporate credit rating and its BB-minus rating on Rexene Corp's $175 million senior notes due 2004 on CreditWatch with "developing" implications, meaning ratings could be raised or lowered.
This action follows the initiation of a proxy contest to gain control of Rexene's board of directors. Rexene is a Dallas, Texas-based petrochemical produceer.

Wyser-Pratte & Co Inc and Spear, Leeds & Kellog, which together own about 10.1 percent of Rexene's outstanding common stock, seek the electionof majority of directors who would be committed to considering a previously rejected purchase offer from Huntsman Corp as well as any higher offers by qualified pruchasers.

The replacement of a majority of directors would constitute a "change of control" under the bond indenture and bank credit agreement that would allow these creditors to require the company to repurchase or repay about $240 million of debt, heightening financial risk.
In addition, Rexene management could take defensive actions that could adversely affect current credit quality.
If Rexene were acquried by a rated company, the potential rating implications could vary depending on the credit profile of the combined company.
If Rexene were acquired by Huntsman or another unrated firm, ratings most likely would be withdrawn. Standard & Poor's will continue to monitor developements.
